newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close higher on exports, crush pace.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close higher on exports, crush pace.

text.p: Bullish input from the export and crush sector boosted CBOT soybean futures to a higher close and demand was broad-based, traders said.

"The sales have given buyers confidence. The demand numbers were extremely good everywhere and it was encouraging to see Europe and China taking beans and products," said Mark Cermak, trading specialist for Chicago-based trade house O'Connor and Co.
USDA Friday said for the week ended November 7 U.S. net exports of soybeans totaled 1.118 million tonnes, above expectations for 600,000 to 800,000 tonnes.
The soybean sales pace for this year was at 12.347 million tonnes, above the year-ago pace of 9.998 million.
The government said the net sales for the week were one-quarter above the prior week and five percent above the four-week average.
Major increases of 249,800 tonnes were noted for China with Belgium, the United Kingdom and the Netherlands also key purchasers of U.S. soybeans that week.
Soybeans closed four to 8-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with November up 7-3/4 at $6.99. January closed 8-1/2 cents per bushel higher at $6.96-3/4.
Traders also said the aggressive pace of U.S. soybean crushings contributed to the advance of soybean futures.

The weekly National Oilseeds Processors Association (NOPA) soybean crush data released Thursday showed a record 30.145 million bushels of soybeans were crushed during the week ended November 13. That tally is above the week ago pace of 29.893 million bushels.
Demand for soybean futures was broad-based but the volume was not extremely heavy and the gains were fairly typical of an orderly demand-led rally, the traders said.
"The market has done a good job of consolidating since the report," Cermak said.

Tuesday, the U.S. Agriculture Department released an estimate for the 1996 U.S. soybean crop at 2.403 billion bushels, above an average of analysts' estimate for 2.376 billion. Soybean futures fell sharply in early dealings Tuesday but rallied to a higher close on the strong demand picture for U.S. soybeans and soy products.
Key buyers included Prudential Securities, Refco Inc and Continental Grain each with roughly three million bushels purchased in the January contract, traders said.
Technical indicators were giving off mixed signals.

Key moving averages for the January continued to show bearish flags before Friday's opening but the contract easily broke through first resistance at $6.92-1/4 per bushel where buy stops were hit. Second resistance at $6.98-3/4 proved a more formidable obstacle. The session high of $7.01-1/2 represented a "psychological" barrier, the traders said.
The session high for Nearby November was $7.02 and the buying waned near that level too, they said.

Short term indictors showed the market moving above neutral territory with November's daily nine day relative strength index (RSI) closing 59 points. The market generally considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 63,000 contracts, above the 48,333 traded Thursday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 500 January $7.00 calls at 9-1/2 cents, Prudential Securities bought 600 January $7.00 calls at 11-1/2 to 12 cents, Tenco Inc bought 600 January $7.00 calls and sold 600 January $7.00 puts at 1-1-1/2 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, up from 18,100 Thursday.
